item.title: India and Japan Coast Guards Chart Course for Strengthened Maritime Cooperation | Law-Order
item.description: The Indian and Japanese Coast Guards held a crucial meeting to boost collaboration in maritime search and rescue, pollution response, and law enforcement. The meeting, part of a broader effort to enhance operational coordination, also included discussions on technology use, training, and multilateral maritime engagement.

item.title: Childhood Quarrel Turns Deadly in Maharashtra's Beed District | Law-Order
item.description: A murder in Beed district, Maharashtra, stemming from a childhood quarrel, has led to the arrest of the accused, Vishal Suryavanshi. The victim, Harshad Shinde, a municipal contract labourer, was shot and attacked with a sickle. The accused was arrested while travelling between Kaij and Kalamb tehsil.

item.title: Gurugram Cracks Down on Wrong-Side Driving: 13 Drivers Booked | Law-Order
item.description: The Gurugram Traffic Police have intensified their campaign against wrong-side driving by filing FIRs against 13 offenders. This move follows public awareness efforts and aims to curb increasing violations. Over 2,000 challans have been issued in just two weeks, highlighting the growing concern over traffic rule adherence.

item.title: Minnesota's Legal Battle Against Immigration Crackdown | Law-Order
item.description: A US District Judge in Minnesota is handling legal challenges against the Trump administration's aggressive immigration policies. State officials claim these actions violate constitutional rights, as federal agents have been forcefully detaining individuals based on race, causing public unrest and legal battles.

item.title: Sabri Lamouchi Appointed as Tunisia's New Head Coach | Sports-Games
item.description: Sabri Lamouchi, former manager of Nottingham Forest, has been appointed as Tunisia's national team coach, succeeding Sami Trabelsi after the team's Africa Cup of Nations exit. Lamouchi, also a former coach for Cardiff City and Ivory Coast, will serve until July 31, 2028.

item.title: Kyiv's Cold Crisis: Battling the Dark Winter Amidst Energy Struggles | Headlines
item.description: Emergency crews in Kyiv, Ukraine, are racing to restore power after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure during the coldest winter in years. This has left civilians without electricity and heat, facing harsh conditions. Residents share their challenges, while energy workers and soldiers are hailed as heroes.

item.title: Trump's Immigration Suspension: A New Era of Visa Restrictions | Law-Order
item.description: The Trump administration is suspending immigrant visa processing for 75 countries as part of its aggressive immigration enforcement strategy. The pause, effective January 21, excludes visitor visas and aims to curb welfare reliance by migrants. This move reflects Trump's longstanding commitment to limiting immigration since his return to office.

item.title: Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor Appointed as ITBP Chief Amid Controversy | Law-Order
item.description: Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor, former Haryana Police chief, has been appointed as the director general of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), replacing Praveen Kumar, who becomes head of the Border Security Force (BSF). Kapoor's appointment follows controversy and his relief from the Haryana DGP position.

item.title: Taiwan's Strategic Push for Lower U.S. Tariffs | Politics
item.description: Senior Taiwanese officials, including Vice Premier Cheng Li-chiun, are in Washington to negotiate lower U.S. tariffs on Taiwan's exports and strengthen bilateral investment. Taiwan aims to reduce these tariffs from 20% to 15%. The talks have reached a broad consensus but await further developments.

item.title: Trump's Plan: A New Dawn for Gaza Governance | Law-Order
item.description: The United States is advancing a Gaza ceasefire plan. The next phase involves disarming Hamas, forming a technocratic government in Gaza, and establishing U.S. oversight. Challenges include international security deployment and immense reconstruction needs. Egypt, Turkiye, and Qatar support the initiative headed by Ali Shaath.
